Signature Private Key Management

Signature Private Key Management is a module in the developer tools used to configure digital signing for mini program packages. By configuring an RSA private key file, developers can sign the exported offline code package to ensure its integrity and authenticity.

Access Entry

In the developer tools top menu bar, select Settings > Signature Private Key Management to open the management panel.

Interface Description

The Signature Private Key Management panel contains the following elements:

Element Description
Private Key File Path Displays the absolute path of the currently configured private key file. Not shown if unconfigured. A delete button on the right clears the current configuration when clicked.
Need Password A checkbox indicating whether the selected private key is encrypted (protected by a passphrase). When checked, the developer tools will prompt for a password during packaging.
Edit Button Clicking this opens a system file picker dialog. Only .pem or .enc format private key files are accepted. The selection is saved automatically upon confirmation.

Configuration Steps

  1. Click the Edit button. In the file picker dialog, select your RSA private key file (only .pem and .enc formats are supported).
  2. After selection, the private key path will appear on the panel. The configuration is automatically saved to the project's macle.config.json file.
  3. If your private key is passphrase-encrypted, check the Need Password box. Otherwise, leave it unchecked.

Private Key Requirements

  • Algorithm: RSA-3072 (recommended) or other RSA key sizes
  • Format: PEM encoded (.pem) or encrypted PEM encoded (.enc)
  • If the private key is protected by a passphrase, the "Need Password" option must be checked; otherwise, signing will fail due to inability to decrypt the key

Signing Principle

Packaging signature uses the RSA-SHA256 + PSS padding scheme. The process is as follows:

  1. Compute the SHA-256 digest of the ZIP package content (output as a hexadecimal string)
  2. Sign the digest using the configured RSA private key with RSA_PKCS1_PSS_PADDING padding mode
  3. Write the Base64-encoded signature result to a <zip-filename>.sign file in the same directory as the ZIP package

Signing During Packaging

When executing the packaging operation, the developer tools automatically checks whether a valid private key is configured:

  • Configured and file exists: The ZIP package is signed directly using the private key, generating a .sign file.
  • Configured but file missing / not configured: A prompt appears indicating the signature file is not configured or is abnormal. You can choose to go to the Signature Private Key Management panel to set it up, or cancel and proceed with unsigned packaging.
  • "Need Password" checked: Before signing, a password input dialog will appear. The correct passphrase must be provided to complete the signing.

Storage Location

The signature configuration is stored in the macle.config.json file at the project root. Relevant fields:

{
  "privateKeyPath": "/path/to/your/private-key.pem",
  "needPassword": false
}
Field Type Description
privateKeyPath String Absolute path to the private key file. Empty means not configured.
needPassword Boolean Whether a passphrase is required to decrypt the private key. Defaults to false.

Notes

  • Tip: Keep your private key file secure and do not commit it to source code repositories.
  • Tip: After changing the private key, existing .sign files from previous builds will no longer match the new key. Re-package and re-sign to regenerate them.
  • Tip: If you don't need signing, clear the private key file path or remove the privateKeyPath field from the configuration. Packaging will then skip the signing step.
  • Tip: The signing process does not modify the original ZIP file. It generates an additional .sign file alongside it.
